Queuewe
Avigail Bahat | Senior product designer | Take-home task

Queuewe

Book a session and get notified on any changes.

Main features:

  1. Choose a slot: visitors pick a time from the manager's schedule.
  2. Live status: visitors always see when their session starts.
  3. Change notifications: when a session runs late or changes, every waiting visitor sees it right away.
  4. Session control: the manager starts, ends or extends each session.
Overview

From a shared sheet to a live queue

Parent-teacher meetings usually run on a shared Google Sheet, so nobody knows the wait or hears about changes.

Queuewe is an app for 1:1 sessions. A manager creates a schedule of slots for sessions. A visitor books a slot, watches the live queue move until it's their time.

The rule: the queue always matches what is happening, and everyone sees a late or early session right away.

Manager (Teacher or staff)

Creates the schedule, shares the link, and runs each session: start, extend, delay or cancel.

Visitor (Parent)

Books a slot and waits for their turn. Always sees the live status, and can change the slot until the manager's cutoff.

The research behind this is in the appendix.

Manager features

Set up and run the queue

Key need: the manager must create a schedule, know what's happening and keep the queue moving.

Must haveNice to haveLater
  1. Create a schedule: preset or from scratch, slot time and days
  2. Share the schedule link
  3. See the schedule and who is now
  4. Start, end or extend the session
  5. Delay the queue
  6. Notification when the session is almost up
  7. Cancel the queue
  1. Adjust the day: block a slot, add time, take a break, or call the next visitor early
  2. Edit the queue: reorder, add a visitor, skip one who doesn't show up, or close it to new visitors
  3. Queue settings: virtual or physical meeting, and when changes are accepted
  4. Save drafts and export a schedule
  5. Create a schedule with AI
  6. Connect a calendar or booking service, such as Google Calendar
  1. Waiting list, and queue setup on an outside service
  2. Live vs. non-live queue setting
  3. Analytics
  4. Customize the look of the waiting screen: colors, fonts, and more
  5. Swipe to check in a visitor

The research behind this is in the appendix.

Summary

Summary and next steps

I chose to focus on parent-teacher meetings and spent most of the task designing for the visitor: booking and the live queue. The manager side is scoped, with the first step of schedule setup designed.

  • The problem: parent-teacher meetings run on a shared Google Sheet, with no live position and no notifications.
  • Main strengths of the solution: a lock screen widget that gives the visitor a live view of the queue, and a home screen built around the upcoming session. Live notifications and queue changes are a clear step up from the shared sheet.
  • Next: the manager experience, such as how a manager checks visitors in and out, and what happens when someone doesn't show up.

Thanks for reading. Happy to walk through any of this live.

Appendix

Research: competitors and users

The brief was open, so I spent a day researching competitors and user types.

Competitors

  • QueueBee, queue management for customer waiting lines
  • QRQ, queue management and virtual queue software
  • Queue App, virtual waiting list (Google Play)
  • Clalit, queue and waiting-list setup on an outside service
  • Calendly, meeting scheduling
  • Google Calendar, calendar with appointment schedules

Users

  • Parent-Teacher talk
  • Salon
  • Gov service
  • Medical clinic
  • Buy tickets to something
  • Consultation
  • Hairdresser
  • Restaurant
  • Experience (art exhibit)
  • Viewer
